subject: Physics
title: Grade 9 Olympiad Mechanics Conceptual Ontology & Dependency Graph

structural_pillars.name: Inertial Reference Frames & Galilean Invariance
structural_pillars.statement: An inertial frame is one in which Newton's 1st Law holds without fictitious forces. If the vector sum of external forces is zero, velocity is invariant: Sigma F = 0 <=> v = const.
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Valid in any frame moving at constant velocity relative to an inertial reference; invalid in accelerating or rotating frames without D'Alembert pseudo-forces.

structural_pillars.name: System Demarcation & Internal Force Cancellation
structural_pillars.statement: By Newton's 3rd Law, all internal forces between particles in an isolated system sum to zero pairwise. Only external forces alter the motion of the center of mass.
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Requires unambiguous system boundary declaration. Never include an internal force on a Free-Body Diagram.

structural_pillars.name: Orthogonal Vector Decomposition & Coordinate Independence
structural_pillars.statement: Newton's 2nd Law holds independently along any set of mutually orthogonal axes. The acceleration along any axis is governed strictly by the net force component along that axis.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: \Sigma F_x = m a_x, \quad \Sigma F_y = m a_y, \quad \Sigma F_z = m a_z
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Coordinate axes should align with the direction of acceleration or constraint surface to decouple equations.

structural_pillars.name: Kinematic Invariants & String-Pulley Constraints
structural_pillars.statement: For ideal inextensible strings and massless frictionless pulleys, the total length of the string is invariant, yielding a strict geometric constraint linking accelerations.
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Tension is uniform throughout an ideal light string; pulleys must have negligible moment of inertia and friction.

structural_pillars.name: Non-Holonomic Friction Thresholds & State Branching
structural_pillars.statement: Friction is a self-adjusting constraint force that switches regimes at the limiting static threshold: static if driving force is below threshold, kinetic if relative slip occurs.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: f_s \le \mu_s N \quad \text{(Static equilibrium)}, \quad f_k = \mu_k N \quad \text{(Dynamic slipping)}
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Normal force N is determined dynamically by perpendicular equilibrium; never assume N = mg without verification.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A sustained net force is required to keep a body in constant velocity (Aristotelian view).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Zero net force maintains constant velocity (Newton's 1st Law). Forces are only required to change velocity (accelerate).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: A puck sliding on an air hockey table or dry ice on glass continues moving indefinitely without propulsion.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: If Action equals Reaction, they must cancel each other out, making acceleration impossible.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Action and Reaction act on strictly distinct bodies. Acceleration of any single body depends only on forces acting ON that body.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: A horse pulls a cart: the cart accelerates because the forward pull of the horse exceeds the friction on the cart's wheels.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Normal reaction N always equals mg.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Normal force is an adjusting constraint force: on an incline N = mg cos theta; in an accelerating elevator N = m(g +- a).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Weighing an object on a scale inside an elevator accelerating upward shows a reading greater than mg.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Friction always acts in the direction opposite to the object's velocity in the lab frame.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Friction opposes relative motion between contacting surfaces. It can accelerate an object forward (e.g. car drive wheels, walking, top block on moving cart).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: When walking forward, the shoe pushes backward on the ground; static friction pushes forward on the shoe, accelerating the person.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Static friction is always equal to mu_s * N.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Static friction is a self-adjusting inequality: 0 <= f_s <= mu_s * N. It matches the applied force exactly until slipping occurs.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Pushing gently on a heavy wardrobe with 5 N results in exactly 5 N of static friction, not 500 N.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Heavier objects fall faster because gravity pulls on them with greater force.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Gravitational force F = mg is proportional to mass, but inertial resistance to acceleration a = F/m is inversely proportional to mass, yielding invariant a = g.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Galileo's Leaning Tower experiment and Apollo 15 hammer-feather drop on the Moon in a vacuum.
